source_snapshot.procedure: Change different Daylight saving time settings; generic setup says clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: The displayed date/time changes after setting daylight saving time.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL proposes a WebUI enable/disable/offset change and time readback, but treats DST as a generic clock shift and omits zone/rule/transition, expected UTC behavior, repeated/skipped local time, affected clock surfaces, NTP interaction and restoration.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires a documented timezone/DST matrix, normalized WebUI/API/SEL reads, NTP handling, preserved event boundaries and policy restoration.

old_problem: `Different DST` and `time will change` do not identify whether the source asks only to apply supported DST configurations or to prove actual transition-boundary behavior. An arbitrary toggle can shift audit presentation without showing the documented rule, may corrupt chronology, and cannot reveal whether UTC, local display, SEL timestamps or NTP-owned clocks changed.
disposition_reason: Preserve the source's setting-change objective as an explicit matrix of Project-supported DST states for one authoritative timezone: at minimum approved disabled and enabled/rule states, each with exact offset, visual WebUI save/readback, normalized clock observations and restoration. This validates configuration application only. A real spring-forward/fall-back boundary is credited solely when separately declared and executed with authoritative transition instants and skipped/repeated-local-time acceptance; it is never inferred from a toggle. Missing timezone/rule values are safe runtime parameters rather than an open engineering decision.
decision_basis: XLSX row 919, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest, adjacent absolute-time/timezone cases and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed.
DST is a zone rule applied to local representation, not a generic instruction to change the underlying UTC instant; the Project must bind the actual rule and affected clock surfaces.
The source requires a real setting change, so WebUI visual evidence, audit confirmation and before/after normalized time are retained; passive observation or IPMI-only evidence cannot substitute.
Configuration-state coverage and real transition-boundary coverage have different prerequisites and expected results; recording that boundary prevents a false full-DST claim.

test_case.test_name: Verify supported BMC daylight-saving configuration states and declared transition scope
test_case.purpose: Verify each approved BMC WebUI DST configuration state for the selected timezone visibly saves the exact enabled/disabled rule and offset, produces the documented local-time presentation while preserving the expected UTC/event relationship, follows NTP policy and restores the original configuration; explicitly distinguish this from any separate real transition-boundary qualification.
required_package: Exact BMC asset/firmware/WebUI identity and vendor-documented DST controls, affected clock surfaces and NTP interaction
Authoritative timezone, DST rule/version, enabled/disabled states, offset and Project-approved expected local/UTC mapping
Numeric time tolerance, observation interval and declared scope: configuration-state only or separately specified spring/fall transition boundaries
For transition scope only, exact transition instants plus expected skipped/repeated local times and event-order acceptance
Authorized WebUI operator, trusted reference and supported vendor API/IPMI/SEL comparison methods
Time-sensitive impact approval, preserved audit/SEL evidence and original timezone/DST/NTP restoration plan
test_case.test_command: STATE-CHANGING MANUAL WEBUI TEST; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT PER-STATE APPROVAL. Preserve logs and capture the verified WebUI timezone/DST/NTP baseline plus normalized supported clock surfaces. Build explicit rows for every approved DST state, including disabled and enabled/rule/offset states actually supported. For one row, capture before UI, obtain approval, save exactly that DST configuration once, capture entered rule/offset, confirmation and audit event, then re-open and compare local display, UTC-normalized reference, documented API/IPMI/SEL surfaces and NTP behavior within tolerance. Restore baseline before another row. Do not alter absolute time to fake a DST transition. Credit spring/fall transition coverage only through a separately approved boundary procedure with exact instants and skipped/repeated-time checks. Never clear logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: Each supported approved state is visibly saved and read back with the exact rule/offset; local time changes by the documented amount relative to the stable reference or behaves exactly as the vendor clock model specifies, while UTC/event chronology and NTP behavior satisfy the approved policy. The original configuration is restored. Results state CONFIGURATION-STATE COVERAGE unless separately evidenced transition-boundary rows pass; no boundary behavior is inferred from toggling.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS for a configuration row requires exact WebUI before/save/after evidence, correct rule/offset, normalized observed-versus-expected local/UTC result, audit boundary, NTP policy and successful restoration. A generic visible clock change, save toast or one IPMI read cannot pass. Wrong/unsupported rule, incorrect offset, unexpected UTC/SEL mutation, chronology problem, NTP overwrite or restoration failure is FAIL and stops. Missing zone/rule/tolerance/approval/recovery is NOT READY. Transition PASS additionally requires the specified spring/fall instants and skipped/repeated-local-time evidence.
safety_gate: Do not clear or rewrite SEL/audit logs; preserve the event boundary through each configuration change and restoration.
Verify exact target, timezone, rule and UI state; do not use arbitrary `different` settings or substitute an IPMI-only action for WebUI coverage.
Do not change absolute time, host time, timezone or NTP unless explicitly part of the approved row; never fake transition coverage.
Assess certificate, token, schedule, power-action and audit-consumer impacts and obtain approval before each save.
Stop on ambiguous clock effects, invalid/rejected rule, unexpected sync override or chronology damage; do not save again or advance automatically.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware identity, authoritative timezone/rule/version/state matrix, tolerance/NTP policy, declared coverage level and impact approval
Per-state visual before/entered/save/after WebUI captures with exact enabled/rule/offset values and BMC audit record
Trusted reference plus normalized WebUI and documented vendor API/IPMI/SEL values before, immediately after and settled
Expected-versus-observed local/UTC/offset result, NTP behavior and first post-change event chronology
For separately declared transition scope, exact boundary timestamps and skipped/repeated local-time plus event-order evidence
Baseline restoration, preserved logs, no-retry proof and engineer verdict with explicit coverage label
test_case.recovery: On wrong rule/offset, unexpected clock mutation, sync overwrite or chronology impact, stop and preserve UI/audit/SEL evidence. Restore the original DST/timezone/NTP policy through the verified WebUI only after fresh authorization, then re-read all documented surfaces. Do not alter absolute time, clear logs or repeat the failed state as an automatic retry.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently test DST-setting impact. The open-ended wording is resolved into supported configuration rows while explicitly limiting unproven transition coverage; no competing source target remains.

blocked.reason: The configuration matrix, coverage boundary, evidence and recovery are defined. Exact zone/rule/offset/tolerance are Project execution parameters.
